#Import data


#CEA for full sample

```{r}
#Subset a dataframe with all timestamps (key press) and corresponding words for each individual of each video
dat4segmag = dat.cleaned %>% dplyr::select(subjectID,video,timestamp,word,type)
length = movie$length
vid = movie$video
dat4segmag$subjectID= as.factor(as.character(dat4segmag$subjectID))
```

```{r}
movie_filtered = dat4segmag %>% filter (video == vid[1])
segmag1[[1]] <- segmag(movie_filtered$subjectID, movie_filtered$timestamp, time_min=0, time_max=length(vid[1]), gauss_sd = 0.8)
```


## Find the critical events and their windows for each video   
```{r}

set.seed(36448)
movielist = list()
segmag1=list()
critical_cutoff=list()
for (i in 1:9) {
      movie_filtered = dat4segmag %>% filter (video == vid[i])
      segmag1[[i]] <- segmag(movie_filtered$subjectID, movie_filtered$timestamp, time_min=0, time_max=length[i], gauss_sd = 0.8)
      critical_cutoff[[i]] <- bootstrap_critical_cutoffs(segmag1[[i]],500, .95) 
      eb_times <- get_eb_times(segmag1[[i]], critical_cutoff[[i]])
      movielist[[i]] = eb_times
}

check=as.data.frame(segmag1[[1]][["time_keypresses"]])

movielist12 = setNames(movielist, vid)
a= as.data.frame(unlist(movielist12 , recursive = TRUE, use.names = TRUE))

critical.events = setDT(a, keep.rownames = TRUE)[]
critical.events$rn = as.character(substr(critical.events$rn, 1, 9))

b=unlist(segmag1[[1]])
names(critical.events)[1:2] = c("video","timestamp")
```

```{r}
#export list of critical events
write.csv(critical.events,"Processed Data/Level1_output/full_CEA_criticalEvents.csv")
#This version contains 88 CE.
```

```{r}
#plotting critical events
for (j in 1:9){
  plot(segmag1[[j]], critical_cutoff[j], movielist[[j]],  main = paste(vid[j], "with a critical cutoff of 0.95"),cex = 0.5)
}
```

****manual merging to produce the final CE list***
- merging of CE (output: full_mod_CEA_criticalEvents.csv)
  - Overlapping CEs within 800ms threshold are merged into the average value
  - the average value is rounded off to similar decimal place as the overlapping CE to ensure transition to ms.

  
```{r}
##find the windows of these critical events
critical.events.merged=read.csv("Processed Data/Level1_output/full_mod_CEA_criticalEvents.csv")#Read in the manually-modified version of CE list
critical.events.merged=critical.events.merged[,-1] #remove redundant column
#After merging, we have 75 CE left.
critical.events.merged$video = as.character(critical.events.merged$video)
critical.events.merged$timestamp= critical.events.merged$timestamp * 100 
```

```{r}
set.seed(36448)
datalist = list()
for (i in 1:9) {
      movie_filtered = dat4segmag %>% filter (video == movies[i])
      segmag1 <- segmag(movie_filtered$subjectID, movie_filtered$timestamp, time_min=0, time_max=length[i],gauss_sd = 0.8)
      changeOfpoints = segmag1[["data"]][["segmentation_magnitude"]]
      MV1 = cpt.meanvar(changeOfpoints,test.stat='Exponential',method='PELT', penalty='Manual',pen.value= '0.045*log(n)') #identify changes in means and variance
      cps = MV1@cpts
      m = filter(critical.events.merged,grepl(vid[i],video))
      window = list()
      for (j in 1:nrow(m)) {
        a = (cps-m$timestamp[j]) 
        w = match(c(max(a[a <= 0]),min(a[a>=0])),a) #find the maximum negative value and minimum positive value 
        v = as.data.frame(t(array(cps[c(w)])))
        v$event = m$video[j]
        v$timestamp = m$timestamp[j]
        window[[j]] = v
        
#plotting
      }
      datalist[[i]] = window
      plot(MV1,cpt.width=1, main = paste(vid[i],"audio with a penalty of 0.045*log(n)"))
}
 
#open the list twice so we can get to the dataframes 
a = do.call(rbind,datalist)
a = do.call(rbind,a)
```

```{r}
#The process creates some repeated lines. We will remove those replicates.
windows = unique(a)
names(windows)[1] = "event_start"
names(windows)[2] = "event_end"
names(windows)[3]="video" 
windows<-windows[order(windows[,'video']),]
unique_window=unique(windows[c("event_start","event_end")])
#We have 73 unique windows, which suggests that 1 pairs of CE shared overlapping windows.

#To distinguish these CEs, we will split each overlapping window from its middle point to create  distinct windows for each CE.
which(duplicated(windows$event_start))
#pair 1: 1507, 1763, 1861 (window: 1416-2009) video 645255968
#we'll divide the window into three separate windows
windows[67,2]=1613
windows[68,1]=1614
windows[68,2]=1811
windows[69,1]=1812

unique_window=unique(windows[c("event_start","event_end")])
#Now we have distinct windows for all 75 CEs.

```


## Find whether each event is identified or not by each participant 
```{r, warning=FALSE}
windows = read.csv(file = "Processed Data/Level1_output/full_CEA_Windows.csv")#read in the CEs and their windows
windows = windows[,-1] #Remove the irrelevant first column 


idat = dat4segmag #list of timestamps for each participant
idat$timestamp = idat$timestamp * 100 #converting timestamp to ms
windows$video = as.integer(windows$video)
subjID = unique(as.character(idat$subjectID)) #generate a list of subjectIDs
vlist = list() 
biglist = list()

#Find out the CE identified by each subject
for (i in 1:length(subjID)){ 
  d = filter(idat, subjectID == subjID[i]) #extract all timestamps for both control and emotion videos for this subject [i]
  for (j in 1:length(vid)){
    d.w = filter(windows, grepl(movies[j], video)) #filter critical event and windows relevant for emotion video [j]
    d.w$event.n = 1:nrow(d.w) #mark the critical events with order
    d.d = filter(d,video == vid[j]) #extract subject [i]'s timestamps and word for emotion video [j]
    d.d = d.d %>% left_join(d.w, by = c("video" = "video")) %>%  #join the subject[i]'s timestamps with the critical events (e.g. there are 7 critical events, then one timestamp by subject[i] will be mapped for 7 times, corresponding to all critical events)
      mutate(event.n = if_else(timestamp.x >= event_start & timestamp.x <= event_end, 
      as.character(event.n), NA_character_)) %>%  #mutate event.n to reflect whether the specific CE marked by event.n is captured by the subject [i]
      arrange(event.n) %>% #rearrange event.n to place all the non-captured CE to the abck
      distinct(timestamp.x, video, .keep_all = T) %>% #remove the redundant timestamps by subject[i] generated by the joining step
      filter(!is.na(event.n)) #filter out the non-captured CE
    vlist[[j]] = d.d
  }
  biglist[[i]] = vlist
}

a = do.call(rbind,biglist)
a = do.call(rbind,a)
```

```{r}
names(a)[3] = "Timestamp"
names(a)[8] = "Critical_Event_Timestamp"

#check if any subject did not identify ANY critical event
subjID2 <- filter(a, type=="emotion") 
subjID2 <- unique(as.character(subjID2$subjectID)) #All subject identify at least one CE
```

```{r}
#write.csv(a, "Processed Data/Level1_output/full_CEA_IdentifiedByIndividuals.csv")
```

## Calculate CEA 
```{r}
#We will now calculate the metric Consensus Event Agreement (CEA). This measures the percentage that an individual has identified the critical events agreed by the group (as identified by segmag).
critical.events.merged=read.csv("Processed Data/Level1_output/full_mod_CEA_criticalEvents.csv")#Read in the manually-modified version of CE list
critical.events.merged$video = as.character(critical.events.merged$video)
critical.events.merged$timestamp= critical.events.merged$timestamp * 100 

#First count the total number of consensus events for each video based on the dataframe "critical_event_merged"
critical.segmag = count(critical.events.merged$video)
names(critical.segmag)[1] = "video"
names(critical.segmag)[2] = "consensus"

#Excluding events that are identified multiple times by the same subjects 
dat.unique = a[!duplicated(a[,c('subjectID','video','event.n')]),]
subjID <- filter(dat.unique, type=="emotion") 
subjID <- unique(as.character(subjID$subjectID))

#check if the final output still contain 57 distinct CE and windows
test_v =  unique(dat.unique[c("event_start","event_end")])

```

```{r}
#Find the total number of consensus events identified by each subject for a given video
dat.group = dat.unique %>% group_by(video, type, subjectID) %>% tally()

#Map the total consensus event identified by the segmag 
dat.consensus = merge(dat.group, critical.segmag, by="video") #Introduce the new variable "consensus" which is the # of CE for each video

# It is calculated as the total number of critical events hit by the subject for a given filem / the sum of consensus events identified by segmag for a given film.
dat.consensus$CEA = dat.consensus$n/dat.consensus$consensus 

cond=read.csv("Processed Data/Level0_output/ES_Language_LowEffortRemoved.csv")
cond <- unique(dplyr::select(cond, c(subjectID,condition)))
dat.consensus<- left_joint(dat.consensus,cond)
```

```{r}
#write.csv(dat.consensus,"Processed Data/Level1_output/full_CEA.csv")
```

```{r}
seg.critical.events.merged=seg.critical.events.merged[,-1] #remove redundant column
#After merging, we have 82 CE left.
seg.critical.events.merged$video = as.character(seg.critical.events.merged$video)
seg.critical.events.merged$timestamp= seg.critical.events.merged$timestamp * 100 
```

```{r}
set.seed(36448)
datalist = list()
for (i in 1:9) {
      movie_filtered = seg.dat4segmag %>% filter (video == movies[i])
      segmag1 <- segmag(movie_filtered$subjectID, movie_filtered$timestamp, time_min=0, time_max=length[i],gauss_sd = 0.8)
      changeOfpoints = segmag1[["data"]][["segmentation_magnitude"]]
      MV1 = cpt.meanvar(changeOfpoints,test.stat='Exponential',method='PELT', penalty='Manual',pen.value= '0.045*log(n)') #identify changes in means and variance
      cps = MV1@cpts
      m = filter(seg.critical.events.merged,grepl(vid[i],video))
      window = list()
      for (j in 1:nrow(m)) {
        a = (cps-m$timestamp[j]) 
        w = match(c(max(a[a <= 0]),min(a[a>=0])),a) #find the maximum negative value and minimum positive value 
        v = as.data.frame(t(array(cps[c(w)])))
        v$event = m$video[j]
        v$timestamp = m$timestamp[j]
        window[[j]] = v

##Notes on penalty value: number set based on already detected critical events (merged according to 800ms threshold); smaller - more sensitive to change of points, hence producing varied windows that are not overlapping (i.e. same window containing multiple CEs). In other words, now we have really tight windows that may exclude more participant-generated-segels since they are more likely to fall off the range.
#- by 0.045 penalty, all windows distinguished

        
#plotting
        
      }
      datalist[[i]] = window
      plot(MV1,cpt.width=1, main = paste(vid[i],"audio with a penalty of 0.045*log(n)"))
}
 
#open the list twice so we can get to the dataframes 
a = do.call(rbind,datalist)
a = do.call(rbind,a)
```

##Find whether each event is identified or not by each participant 
```{r, warning=FALSE}
seg.windows = read.csv(file = "Processed Data/Level1_output/seg_CEA_Windows.csv")#read in the CEs and their windows
seg.windows = seg.windows[,-1] #Remove the irrelevant first column 


seg.idat = seg.dat4segmag #list of timestamps for each participant
seg.idat$timestamp = seg.idat$timestamp * 100 #converting timestamp to ms
seg.windows$video = as.integer(seg.windows$video)
seg.subjID = unique(as.character(seg.idat$subjectID)) #generate a list of subjectIDs
vlist = list() 
biglist = list()

#Find out the CE identified by each subject
for (i in 1:length(seg.subjID)){ 
  d = filter(seg.idat, subjectID == seg.subjID[i]) #extract all timestamps for both control and emotion videos for this subject [i]
  for (j in 1:length(vid)){
    d.w = filter(seg.windows, grepl(movies[j], video)) #filter critical event and windows relevant for emotion video [j]
    d.w$event.n = 1:nrow(d.w) #mark the critical events with order
    d.d = filter(d,video == vid[j]) #extract subject [i]'s timestamps and word for emotion video [j]
    d.d = d.d %>% left_join(d.w, by = c("video" = "video")) %>%  #join the subject[i]'s timestamps with the critical events (e.g. there are 7 critical events, then one timestamp by subject[i] will be mapped for 7 times, corresponding to all critical events)
      mutate(event.n = if_else(timestamp.x >= event_start & timestamp.x <= event_end, 
      as.character(event.n), NA_character_)) %>%  #mutate event.n to reflect whether the specific CE marked by event.n is captured by the subject [i]
      arrange(event.n) %>% #rearrange event.n to place all the non-captured CE to the abck
      distinct(timestamp.x, video, .keep_all = T) %>% #remove the redundant timestamps by subject[i] generated by the joining step
      filter(!is.na(event.n)) #filter out the non-captured CE
    vlist[[j]] = d.d
  }
  biglist[[i]] = vlist
}

a = do.call(rbind,biglist)
a = do.call(rbind,a)
```

## Calculate CEA 
```{r}
#We will now calculate the metric Consensus Event Agreement (CEA). This measures the percentage that an individual has identified the critical events agreed by the group (as identified by segmag).
seg.critical.events.merged=read.csv("Processed Data/Level1_output/SEG_mod_CEA_criticalEvents.csv")#Read in the manually-modified version of CE list
seg.critical.events.merged$video = as.character(seg.critical.events.merged$video)
seg.critical.events.merged$timestamp= seg.critical.events.merged$timestamp * 100 

#First count the total number of consensus events for each video based on the dataframe "critical_event_merged"
seg.critical.segmag = count(seg.critical.events.merged$video)
names(seg.critical.segmag)[1] = "video"
names(seg.critical.segmag)[2] = "consensus"

#Excluding events that are identified multiple times by the same subjects 
seg.dat.unique = a[!duplicated(a[,c('subjectID','video','event.n')]),]
seg.subjID <- filter(seg.dat.unique, type=="emotion") 
seg.subjID <- unique(as.character(seg.subjID$subjectID))

#check if the final output still contain 82 distinct CE and windows
test_v =  unique(seg.dat.unique[c("event_start","event_end")])

```

```{r}
#Find the total number of consensus events identified by each subject for a given video
seg.dat.group = seg.dat.unique %>% group_by(video, type, subjectID) %>% tally()

#Map the total consensus event identified by the segmag 
seg.dat.consensus = merge(seg.dat.group, seg.critical.segmag, by="video") #Introduce the new variable "consensus" which is the # of CE for each video

# It is calculated as the total number of critical events hit by the subject for a given filem / the sum of consensus events identified by segmag for a given film.
seg.dat.consensus$CEA = seg.dat.consensus$n/seg.dat.consensus$consensus 
seg.dat.consensus$condition="NoLabel"

#write.csv(seg.dat.consensus,"Processed Data/Level1_output/SEG_CEA.csv")
```
